'''Nicholas John Higham''' (25 December 1961 – 20 January 2024) was a British [[Numerical analysis|numerical analyst]].<ref name="whoswho_2013">{{cite web |url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U45539/ |title=HIGHAM, Prof. Nicholas John', Who's Who 2013, A & C Black, an imprint of Bloomsbury Publishing plc, 2013; online edn, Oxford University Press }}</ref> He was Royal Society Research Professor and [[Richardson Professor of Applied Mathematics]] in the [[Department of Mathematics, University of Manchester|Department of Mathematics]] at the [[University of Manchester]].<ref name="uom">{{cite web|url=http://www.maths.manchester.ac.uk/~higham/|title=Nick Higham - School of Mathematics, University of Manchester|website=www.maths.manchester.ac.uk |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108232454/https://www.maths.manchester.ac.uk/~higham/ |archive-date=2021-01-08 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="googlescholar">{{GoogleScholar|EYlMkOgAAAAJ}}</ref><ref name="mathgene"/><ref name="scopus">{{Scopus|id=7003377200}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2018/03/royal-society-research-professorships-announced/|title=Leading scientists awarded Royal Society Research Professorships|website=royalsociety.org|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-10-09}}</ref>

==Early life and career==
Nicholas John Higham was born in [[Salford]] on 25 December 1961.<ref name="whoswho_2014">{{cite web |url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U45539 |title=HIGHAM, Prof. Nicholas John |work=Who's Who 2014, A & C Black, an imprint of Bloomsbury Publishing plc, 2014; online edn, Oxford University Press }}{{subscription required}}</ref> He was educated at Eccles Grammar School, Eccles College, and the [[University of Manchester]], from which he gained his B.Sc. in mathematics (1982), M.Sc. in Numerical Analysis and Computing (1983), and PhD in Numerical Analysis (1985).<ref name="whoswho_2013"/><ref name="highamphd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Nicholas|last=Higham |title=Nearness Problems in Numerical Linear Algebra |publisher=University of Manchester |year= 1985 |url=http://ethos.bl.uk/OrderDetails.do?uin=uk.bl.ethos.374580|author-link=Nicholas Higham}}</ref> His PhD thesis was supervised by George Hall.<ref name="mathgene"/> He was appointed lecturer in mathematics at the University of Manchester in 1985, where he has been [[Richardson Professor of Applied Mathematics]] since 1998.<ref name="uom" />

In 1988–1989 he was Visiting Assistant Professor of Computer Science at Cornell University, Ithaca, New York.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.research.manchester.ac.uk/portal/nick.higham.html |title= Prof Nicholas Higham FRS {{!}} The University of Manchester |website= www.research.manchester.ac.uk |language=en |access-date=2018-10-17}}</ref>

==Research==
Higham is best known for his work on the accuracy and stability of numerical algorithms.<ref name="acc">{{cite book|url=http://bookstore.siam.org/ot80|title=Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms|author=Higham, Nicholas J.|publisher=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|year=2002|isbn=978-0-89871-521-7|location=Second Edition, Philadelphia}}</ref> He has more than 140 refereed publications<ref name="googlescholar" /><ref name="scopus" /> on topics such as rounding error analysis, linear systems, least squares problems, matrix functions and nonlinear matrix equations, matrix nearness problems, condition number estimation, and generalized eigenvalue problems. He has contributed software to [[LAPACK]] and the [[Numerical Algorithms Group|NAG library]], and has contributed code included in the [[MATLAB]] distribution.

Higham's books include  ''Functions of Matrices: Theory and Computation'' (2008),<ref>{{cite book|url=http://bookstore.siam.org/ot104|title=Functions of Matrices: Theory and Computation|author=Higham, Nicholas J.|publisher=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|year=2008|isbn=978-0-89871-646-7|location=Philadelphia}}</ref>''Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms'',<ref name="acc" /> ''Handbook of Writing for the Mathematical Sciences'',<ref>{{Cite book|last=Higham|first=Nicholas J. |title=Handbook of writing for the mathematical sciences |date=2020 |isbn=978-1-61197-610-6 |edition=Third |location=Philadelphia |oclc=1131865845}}</ref> and ''MATLAB Guide'', co-authored with his brother [[Desmond Higham]].<ref>{{Cite book|last=Higham |first=Desmond J. |title=MATLAB guide|date=2017 |author2=Nicholas J. Higham |isbn=978-1-61197-465-2 |edition=Third |location=Philadelphia |oclc=957339736}}</ref> He was Editor of the ''Princeton Companion to Applied Mathematics''<ref>{{cite book|url=https://press.princeton.edu/titles/10592.html|title=The Princeton Companion to Applied Mathematics|last1=Higham|first1=Nicholas J.|last2=Dennis|first2=Mark R.|last3=Glendinning|first3=Paul|last4=Martin|first4=Paul A.|last5=Santosa|first5=Fadil|last6=Tanner|first6=Jared|publisher=Princeton University Press|year=2015|isbn=9780691150390}}</ref> and a contributor to the ''Penguin Dictionary of Mathematics''.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://www.penguinrandomhouse.com/books/293197/the-penguin-dictionary-of-mathematics-by-david-nelson/9780141030234|title=Penguin Dictionary of Mathematics|last=Nelson|first=David|date=2008-10-02|publisher=Penguin Adult |isbn=9780141030234}}</ref> His books have been translated into Chinese, Japanese and Korean.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Sūri kagaku ronbun handobukku|date=1994|publisher=日本評論社|author=Higham, N.J. |translator=Okumura, Shōji |translator2=Hasegawa, Takemitsu |isbn=978-4535782112 |oclc=674217300}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=数学论文写作 Shu xue lun wen xie zuo|last=Higham|first=Nick|date=2016|publisher=科学出版社 Ke xue chu ban she|others=贾志刚, 常亮, 李建波 Zhigang Jia, Liang Chang, Jianbo Li|isbn=9787030513472|location=Beijing|oclc=1050517123}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ajin.to/index.php?salegdno=132&gtype=1&pgurl=shop/sh_goods_view&ctpose=AAGAAB&ctno=327&otype=6&olist=50&|title=대학교재 전문 출판사(도서출판 아진)|last=아진|first=도서출판|website=ajin.to|access-date=2018-10-12}}</ref>

==Professional service==
Higham served as president of the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM) 2017–2018.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/remembering-nick-higham-1961-2024|title=Remembering Nick Higham 1961–2024|magazine=SIAM News|date=1 May 2024}}</ref>

==Death==
Higham died on 20 January 2024 at the age of 62, after an 18 month struggle with a form of blood cancer. <ref name="obit">{{cite news |url=https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/obituary-nicholas-j-higham |title=Obituary: Nicholas J. Higham |publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]] |date=2024-05-01 |author1=Desmond J. Higham|author1-link=Desmond Higham |author2=Françoise Tisseur |author2-link=Françoise Tisseur}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ilasic.org/ilas-net-archive-2024/#:~:text=SUBJECT%3A%20Nick%20Higham%20(1961%2D%2D2024)|website=International Linear Algebra Society|title=ILAS-NET Message no. 2515 SUBJECT: Nick Higham (1961--2024)|date=January 22, 2024}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Higham's honours include the [[Alston Scott Householder|Alston S. Householder]] Award VI, 1987 (for the best PhD thesis in numerical algebra 1984–1987), the 1988 [[Leslie Fox Prize for Numerical Analysis]], a 1999 [[Junior Whitehead Prize]] from the [[London Mathematical Society]], a 2020 [[IMA Gold Medal]],<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-12-10|title=IMA Gold Medal 2020 awarded to Professor Nick Higham|url=https://ima.org.uk/15765/ima-gold-medal-2020-awarded-to-professor-nick-higham/|access-date=2021-03-15|website=IMA|language=en-GB}}</ref> the [https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/lms.ac.uk/files/files/n_higham.pdf 2019 Naylor Prize and Lectureship] by the London Mathematical Society, the [https://sinews.siam.org/Details-Page/an21-prize-spotlight#5 2021 George Pólya Prize for Mathematical Exposition] by the Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics (SIAM), and the [[Hans Schneider Prize in Linear Algebra|2022 Hans Schneider Prize in Linear Algebra]]. Higham held a prestigious [[Royal Society Wolfson Research Merit Award]] (2003–2008). He was elected as a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2007<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20070717173348/http://www.royalsoc.ac.uk/page.asp?tip=1&id=6616 New Fellows and Foreign Members 2007 www.royalsoc.ac.uk]</ref> and as a [[ACM Fellow]] in 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2020 ACM Fellows Recognized for Work that Underpins Today's Computing Innovations|url=https://www.acm.org/media-center/2021/january/fellows-2020|access-date=2021-03-15|website=www.acm.org|language=en}}</ref>  In 2008 he was awarded the [[Fröhlich Prize]] in recognition of 'his leading contributions to numerical linear algebra and numerical stability analysis'.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/default/files/About_Us/news/2008-3%20LMS%20Prizes%20(4%20July).pdf|title=London Mathematical Society Prizes 2008|publisher=London Mathematical Society|date=4 July 2008|access-date=2024-05-18}}</ref> He was elected a Member of [[Academia Europaea]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Higham_Nicholas|title=Academy of Europe: Higham Nicholas|website=www.ae-info.org|access-date=2018-10-09}}</ref> In 2022 he became [[Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://raeng.org.uk/about-us/fellowship/new-fellows-2022/professor-nicholas-higham-freng-frs|title=Professor Nicholas Higham FREng FRS|website=raeng.org.uk|access-date=2022-12-08}}</ref>

Higham was a Fellow of the Institute of Mathematics and Its Applications, a Fellow of the Institute of Engineering and Technology, and a Fellow of the Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics. He was also a Fellow of the [[Alan Turing Institute]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.turing.ac.uk/people/researchers/nick-higham|title=Nick Higham|website=The Alan Turing Institute|language=en|access-date=2018-10-12}}</ref>
